name: THREE CARD BRAG
description: 3-Card Brag is Britain's classic three-card vying game. Blind and seeing betting costs create a fast contest of hand strength, pressure, and nerve.
tagline: Blind pressure. Three cards. One pot.

content.text: 3-Card Brag is Britain's premier vying card game and a direct ancestor of modern poker. Each player receives three cards and competes for a central pot through blind and seeing bets.

Its signature tension is the blind system: a player can bet without looking at their cards for half the cost, keeping both price pressure and psychological pressure on players who have already seen their hands.
Win the pot by showing the best three-card hand or by being the last player remaining after all others have folded.

Players ante, receive three face-down cards, then bet in turn. Blind players pay the lower blind price. Seeing players pay the higher seeing price. A player may fold, call, raise, see their cards, or force a comparison according to table stakes.

items.text: Prial: three cards of the same rank. The prial of threes is traditionally strongest.
Running flush: three consecutive cards in the same suit.
Run: three consecutive cards in mixed suits.
Flush: three cards in the same suit.
Pair: two cards of one rank.
High card: highest card breaks the tie.

content.text: Staying blind can be valuable because it keeps your betting price lower and makes your hand harder to read. The tradeoff is that you are accepting risk without information.

Seeing early gives you better hand knowledge, but it usually doubles your required betting cost. Strong hands should press value; weak seen hands often need discipline because blind opponents can keep the pot expensive.
Brag does not use cumulative point scoring in a normal hand. The pot is awarded to the last remaining player or to the strongest three-card hand at comparison.
The ranking model is hierarchical: prial, running flush, run, flush, pair, then high card. Special table rules can make the prial of threes the highest possible hand.
